evidence: Hor. S. 1.1.69–70: dē tē fābula narrātur
Cic. Att. 5.1.3: sermō isque multus dē tē fuit
terms.comment: With verbs of speaking, writing, hearing and thinking, and in titles: Dē senectūte.

terms.register: in this sense chiefly in comedy, poetry and post-Augustan prose; a few times in Cicero’s letters (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Verg. A. 1.750: multa super Priamō rogitāns
Cic. Att. 16.6.1: hāc super rē scrībam ad tē Rhēgiō (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: quid rīdēs? mūtātō nōmine dē tē fābula narrātur
phrases.english: why are you laughing? change the name, and the story is about you

phrases.latin: ut vēnī in Arpīnās, cum ad mē frāter vēnisset, in prīmīs nōbīs sermō isque multus dē tē fuit
phrases.english: when I reached Arpinum and my brother had come to see me, our first talk, and a long one, was about you
that is about all on country matters

phrases.latin: dīc sōdēs, inquit Fundānius; nam mālō dē meīs pedibus audīre, quam quem ad modum pedēs bētāceōs serī oporteat
phrases.english: “Tell me, please,” said Fundanius, “for I’d rather hear about my feet than about how beet feet ought to be planted”

phrases.latin: Nūlla tam bona est fortūna, dē quā nīl possīs querī.
phrases.english: No luck is so good that you can find nothing in it to complain about.

phrases.latin: multa super Priamō rogitāns, super Hectore multa
phrases.english: asking many things about Priam, many about Hector
